## 1. What was read

**886 research articles** from 32 of the 33 journals on the roster, filtered to `journal article` and excluding reviews, editorials, news, comment and case reports.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 396 | 141 | 91 | 235 | 23 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: cancer -27%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months — queried directly, PubMed returns zero *Nucleic Acids Research* research articles dated 2025-12, and zero *Bioinformatics* in 2024-04, 2025-01, 2025-04 and 2026-03. Those holes are in the source and are reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest, so a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nature 121, Science 94, Nucleic Acids Res 84, Bioinformatics 57, JAMA 38, J Clin Oncol 33.

## 3. The evidence that moved it

**The single most direct refutation on the microbiome thread is from May 2024.**
[38689063](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689063/) (*Nat Med*): microbiome confounders and quantitative profiling
**challenge predicted microbial targets** in colorectal cancer development.
The `neuro-immune-microbiome-axis` thread is the healthiest in this corpus and
the one three separate readers wrongly called as peaking. This is the paper that
should have been used to argue against it, and it predates the thread's first
recorded card by sixteen months. It is a confounding result, not a null: the
targets were predicted from data that could not support them.

**Removing a suppressive population, twice, in one month.** [38758808](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38758808/)
(*Sci Immunol*): TREM2 **deficiency** reprograms intestinal macrophages and
microbiota to enhance anti-PD-1 therapy. [38684922](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38684922/) (*Nat Immunol*):
sepsis-trained macrophages **promote** antitumoural tissue-resident T cells. Two
myeloid states assumed to be immunosuppressive turn out to be either better
removed or already protective. The `suppressive-population-inversion` thread —
which this corpus found only in August 2026, and called the clearest thing the
2025 backfill bought — is running in May 2024.

**And the same month supplies its mirror image.** [38664585](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38664585/) (*Nat Immunol*):
a dietary commensal microbe enhances antitumour immunity by activating tumour
macrophages to sequester iron. The same cell type, in the same journal, in the
same month, as an asset rather than a liability. That is the thread's actual
shape: not that suppressive populations are secretly good, but that the sign is
context-dependent and the field keeps assigning it globally.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

The TREM2 and sepsis-macrophage papers above are the refutations, and they are
filed on `suppressive-population-inversion` rather than here to avoid
double-counting. [38227896](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38227896/) (*Cancer Discov*) is the supporting side of
`immunotherapy-resistance`: TREX1 inactivation unleashes cancer-cell
STING-interferon signalling and promotes antitumour immunity.

### (b) Method credibility

The microbiome-confounders paper is the month's methodological result as well as
its biological one, which is the combination this corpus values most highly: the
reading and the finding are the same object. Its claim is not that a particular
microbial target is wrong but that the profiling method used to nominate targets
across the field cannot distinguish signal from load.
